facts.title: Driving Requirements in Mozambique
facts.description: To legally drive in Mozambique, you need valid vehicle registration papers, a recognized driver's licence (International or English/SADC preferred), and compulsory third-party insurance (SORCA). If the driver is not the owner, a letter of authorization is required.

facts.title: SORCA Insurance
facts.description: Foreign-registered vehicles must have SORCA insurance (third-party liability) to enter Mozambique. It is usually valid for 30 days and can be purchased online or at the border.

facts.title: Temporary Import Permit (TIP)
facts.description: A temporary import permit is required when bringing a foreign vehicle into Mozambique. Officials at the border will stamp it.

facts.title: Vehicle Safety Equipment
facts.description: Recommended equipment includes seat belts for all passengers, reflective triangles, and a fire extinguisher.

facts.title: Importing a Vehicle into Mozambique
facts.description: All vehicles must be registered with Mozambique authorities. Required documents include original registration, purchase invoice, Bill of Lading, passport copy, and NUIT. Used vehicles may require pre-shipment inspection.

facts.title: Border Crossing for Vehicles
facts.description: To cross into Mozambique with a vehicle: present registration papers, SORCA insurance, temporary import permit, and authorization letters if not the owner. Carry reflective triangles and fire extinguisher.

facts.title: Quick Checklist
facts.description: Vehicle registration papers; Valid driver's license; SORCA insurance; Temporary import permit (TIP); Owner authorization letter (if needed); Passport and travel docs; Customs/import documents (if importing).
